title: Ontario Summer Games - Weather Related Schedule Updates for Outdoor Sports - August 1 & 2
content: Due to the forecasted weather system expected to affect the Waterloo Region on Sunday, August 2, competition schedules for the Ontario Summer Games have been proactively adjusted for several outdoor sports to help ensure events can be completed as planned.
Schedule changes have been made to: • Women's Softball - Budd Park, Kitchener
• Men's Softball - Peter Hallman Ball Yard, Kitchener
• Women’s Baseball - Breithaupt Park / Rim Park, Kitchener
• Men’s Baseball - Bechtel Park / Jack Couch Park / Lions Park, Kitchener
• Archery - Fountain Street Soccer Complex, Cambridge
• Field Lacrosse - WLU Alumni Field, Waterloo

Participants, coaches, and spectators are encouraged to review the updated schedules on the respective sport pages for full details on the Games website . Please continue to monitor the Games website for the latest updates and any further schedule changes.

In collaboration with the Ontario Ministry of Sport and Provincial Sport Organizations, organizers worked to minimize disruptions and support a successful competition experience. Supporting operational adjustments have already been made, including volunteer assignments, medical coverage, transportation, meal services, accommodations, and medal ceremonies.
We appreciate the flexibility and teamwork shown by everyone involved as these changes were implemented. Thank you for your understanding and continued support.
For more information: Corporate Communications and Marketing City of Kitchener Media@kitchener.ca

title: Supporting vendors, rebuilding the Kitchener Market: City provides recovery update following July fire
content: The City recognizes the significant impact the July 12 Kitchener Market fire has had on our vendors, their businesses, employees, and families. Today, we are providing an update on the road ahead, and sharing that indoor market operations will likely be impacted for several months while the building undergoes extensive remediation and restoration.

“We know the impact of this fire reaches far beyond the building itself,” said Andrew Sturgess, Director of Business Growth and Entrepreneurship. “Many vendors are dealing with business disruption, lost inventory and uncertainty about the months ahead, and those impacts are being felt by our local businesses and the broader community. The Kitchener Market is more than a building. It supports local businesses, brings people together and is an important part of our community. We understand the seriousness of this situation, and helping the Market recover as quickly as possible is our highest priority.”

Since the fire, City staff have been working with public health officials, insurance representatives, restoration specialists and safety experts to assess the damage and determine the safest path to reopening.

Those assessments confirmed that while the fire was contained to a relatively small area of the building, smoke, soot and other fire-related contaminants spread throughout the facility, including mechanical and ventilation systems. As a result, extensive cleaning, remediation and restoration work is required before indoor operations can safely resume.

“We know this timeline is difficult news for vendors whose businesses depend on the Market,” said Sturgess. “While we can't yet say exactly how long the recovery will take, we know it will be measured in months, not weeks. Our commitment is to keep vendors informed, support them however we can, and move this work forward as quickly and safely as possible.”

Recovery work will include detailed planning and assessments, followed by building remediation, restoration and the reinstallation of vendor spaces and infrastructure. To help keep the project moving forward, vendors have been asked to remove inventory, equipment and other vendor-owned property from the building by August 19.
As the City works with vendors and other partners to develop a roadmap for reopening, Market vendors will not be charged rent during the recovery period.

At the same time, the City continues to support vendors and the community through expanded outdoor market operations and ongoing promotion to help maintain customer awareness and support during the recovery period.
The outdoor Kitchener Market remains open every Saturday, and residents are encouraged to continue supporting local vendors while recovery efforts continue.
For more information: Corporate Communications and Marketing City of Kitchener Media@kitchener.ca

title: City of Kitchener welcomes cricket net partner to Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park
content: The City of Kitchener is pleased to welcome another community partner to the Cowan Recreation Centre  at  RBJ Schlegel Park.

Grow with Nav Inc., a Kitchener based mortgage brokerage,  will contribute  $100,000 over ten years to sponsor the  centre’s newly named ‘Grow Nation Cricket Nets’. Th is partnership reflects a shared commitment to growing sport opportunities and supporting community connection s across Kitchener.

Partnerships like this help us create more opportunities for residents to  participate in the sports and activities they love,” says Mayor Berry Vrbanovic. “Thank you to Grow With Nav Inc. for sponsoring the Grow Nation Cricket Nets. Together with the outdoor cricket amenities at RBJ Schlegel Park, these new indoor nets will help establish the park as a year-round destination for cricket, expanding opportunities for residents to enjoy one of Kitchener’s fastest-growing sports .

The Grow Nation Cricket Nets are the City of Kitchener’s first municipally owned and operated indoor cricket practice nets, featuring an 18-metre lane equipped with a bowling machine for focused skill development, and a 38-metre lane designed for both bowlers and batters to train at full length.

Located within the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park, the Grow Nation Cricket Nets enhance  a state-of-the-art recreation facility designed to support inclusive, diverse and accessible sport and wellness opportunities. Through its wide range of amenities and programming, the facility will serve residents of all ages and abilities while supporting the growth and development of more than 30 local sport organizations.

“Cricket is part of who I am,” says Navjot  Bindra,  Founder of Grow With Nav Inc . “ I grew up with the sport, and now I get to watch my son pick up a bat in the same city where  we're building our life. Sponsoring the cricket  nets is about giving Kitchener's kids and families a place to play the game they love, without leaving the city. For me, this is what growing with your community looks like.”

The Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel  Park is scheduled to open late this year. Projected to attract 10,000 visits in the first year, the cricket nets will be available for booking online later this year and will operate from  6 a.m. to 12 a.m. seven days a week.
To stay  up to date on the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Pa rk, visit  Kitchener.ca and sign-up to receive  an invite to their Grand Opening event.
About RBJ Schlegel Park, home of Cowan Recreation Centre

RBJ Schlegel Park is where sport, recreation, and community come together. As Waterloo Region's premier destination for year-round activity, the park brings together indoor and outdoor spaces where residents of all ages and abilities can connect, compete, and belong.

The Cowan Recreation Centre will welcome more than 500,000 visits annually and support over 30 local  sport organizations. Featuring two pools, a FIFA-sized field house, quad gymnasium, indoor walking track, indoor cricket nets, and flexible community spaces, the facility will increase programming opportunities and support recreation, wellness, tournaments, events, and community connection for generations to come.

title: Equip Sport lockers now available to use at City of Kitchener parks
content: The City of Kitchener  celebrated the installation of thirty  free-to-use sport s  equipment  lockers  this afternoon  as they launched a new partnership with Equip Sport and Canadian Tire Jumpstart Charities  ( Jumpstart ). There are  now  more ways to play in parks across Kitchener as basketballs, soccer balls,  frisbees and other fitness gear are waiting to be borrowed for free from 30 new Equip Sport lockers.

Originally announced on June  9, 2026, during Mayor Berry  Vrbanovic’s  State of the City address, Equip Sport lockers offer  free  self-serve access to  sports equipment. The lockers are secure, easy-to-use, and  support  a shared, community-driven  recreation model in public spaces.

The program is supported through funding from  Canadian Tire Jumpstart Charities (Jumpstart) ,  a national charity supported by Canadian Tire Corporation  dedicated to enabling lifelong success for kids and youth by removing financial,  physical and systemic barriers to sport and play. In partnership with Equip Sport  and local municipalities, Jumpstart is helping bring free access to sports equipment directly into public spaces, making  everyday play more accessible.  The City of Kitchener joins a growing number of municipalities across Canada who are committed to removing barriers so residents of all ages can stay active.

“As people age, some of their  favourite childhood summer  memories  come from  playing pick-up games with friends in  parks in Kitchener and everywhere .  Whether  you’re a kid or a kid at heart, every resident deserves the opportunity to enjoy the benefits of sport and play, regardless of their financial circumstances ,” said Mayor Vrbanovic. “We’re grateful to  Equip Sport and Jumpstart  for  making sports more accessible ,  ensuring residents of all ages can participate in healthy, active lifestyles .”

“Sport has the power to bring kids and communities together, but only if the door is open to everyone,” said  Marco  Di Buono, President, Canadian Tire Jumpstart Charities . “ Together with the City of Kitchener and Equip Sport, we're empowering youth through sport by creating free access to equipment in neighbourhood parks, so more kids and families can play, connect and build community.”

To access equipment and open the locker , users  16 years or older can  download the free Equip Sport app, select the  location and  equipment of their choice, and take a photo of the locker to open it .

After  play, users return the equipment and take a second photo.  Users can rate their  experience or report any issue directly in the app. If an item goes missing, Equip Sport manages replacement of the item at no cost to the municipality.
Thirty Equip Sport  lockers have been installed at the following locations:
*Temporary location.  Will  relocate to Upper Canada Park in 2027

Each location was selected by City staff in partnership with Equip Sport to  reflect  community  interests, park  amenities and support equitable access to equipment across Kitchener. Usage data will be used to determine additional equipment needs and possible future locker locations.
To learn more about Equip Sport  lockers in Kitchener, visit  Kitchener.ca/FreeToPlay .

Quotes "Every child deserves the chance to discover the joy of sport.  We're proud to partner with the City of Kitchener and Canadian Tire Jumpstart to bring free sports equipment to 30 neighbourhood parks, creating a new kind of public infrastructure that makes play as accessible as the park itself. By placing equipment where families already gather, play and connect, we're helping more children build healthy, active habits that last a lifetime.”
Charmaine Crooks, five-time Olympian, Equip Sport Canadian Ambassador

Founded in Switzerland in 2021, Equip Sport is redefining urban sport through free, open-access equipment stations powered by a smartphone app. The model has expanded to more than 500 stations across Europe, 50 in the City of Ottawa and 80 in British Columbia.

title: Have your say in Kitchener: committee and board recruitment now open
content: Kitchener residents have an opportunity to help shape the future of their city as recruitment is now open for volunteer positions on a variety of City advisory committees and boards.

The City is seeking community members from diverse backgrounds and lived experiences to help shape City decisions by sharing their experiences, perspectives and expertise. Advisory committees and boards provide feedback to Council and help ensure local decision-making reflects the voices of the Kitchener community.
Applications are now being accepted for:
Active Transportation and Trails Advisory Committee
Dog and Animal Designation Appeal Committee
Reconciliation, Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Advisory Committee
Volunteers will serve two-year terms and must live, own property or work in Kitchener to be eligible. Applications will be accepted using the City’s online form from July 29 to August 19.
To learn more about available opportunities and apply, visit  Kitchener.ca/Advisory .

title: Support local at the outdoor Kitchener Market on July 25
content: The Kitchener Market will be open this Saturday, July 25, with an outdoor market experience in the Breezeway featuring local farmers, makers and vendors.

While recovery efforts continue inside the Market building, we're pleased to provide an opportunity for the community to shop local and support vendors. Visitors can expect many of the familiar vendors that make the Kitchener Market a community favourite, offering fresh produce, packaged foods and unique local products.

The Kitchener Market has long been an important gathering place and a vital support for local farmers, small businesses and entrepreneurs. We encourage residents to come out, shop local and support the vendors who help make the Market such a special part of our community.

title: Registration is now open for Kitchener’s 3rd annual Paddle Palooza Pickleball Festival
content: Get ready to hit the courts in Downtown Kitchener as the City of Kitchener’s Paddle Palooza Pickleball Festival returns to Carl Zehr Square on Tuesday, August 25 from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m.
Whether you're a seasoned player or new to the game, Paddle Palooza offers friendly competition, learn to play courts, great prizes, and high-energy vibes all day long.
The tournament, presented in partnership with Four Fathers Brewing and Four Fathers Pickleball, offers the following divisions, limited to six teams each:

Registration is now open at  Kitchener.ca/pickleball. The cost to register a team in the tournament is $50 per team with a limit of six teams per division. All other street play is free. Proceeds from the tournament will support the city’s Every Kid Counts program, helping to make camp an option for children and youth in Kitchener by providing inclusion support.

Not quite ready for tournament play or just want to enjoy the game of pickleball? Paddle Palooza will celebrate all levels of pickleball skill and interest, ranging from curious to competitive. Join the free drop-in s treet play (3 courts), learn-to-play, and pick up some tips & tricks. Come out and give pickleball a try.  Spectators are welcome and encouraged. Whether you're playing or just soaking up the vibes, there's something for everyone. Come for the tournament, stay for the fun, including drop-in games, family activities, vendor booths, food trucks, a beer garden and more.

Pickleball is a hybrid paddle sport that combines elements of tennis, badminton, and ping pong, and is experiencing a rapid rise in popularity across Canada, reaching over one million Canadians (Pickleball Canada, 2023). The City of Kitchener has also seen significant growth and interest in the sport in recent years at community centres and outdoor courts.
For more information, or to register a team, visit Kitchener.ca/pickleball .

title: Beloved local restaurant selected to bring a major flavour boost to the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park
content: The City of Kitchener has selected  Almadina, a long-standing, family-run Kitchener business with more than 30 years in the community, to  operate the on-site food service at the new Cowan Recreation Centre, located at RBJ Schlegel park and  opening late this year.

Almadina was chosen following a competitive process that emphasized fresh, nutritious and locally sourced food, diverse and inclusive menu offerings, strong customer experience and a commitment to sustainable operations, including responsible sourcing and waste reduction.

Centrally  located within the Cowan Recreation Centre, the on-site food service will support the facility’s role as a landmark recreation destination for residents, families, athletes and sport tourism events. The menu will include a wide variety of options such as smoothies and juices, flatbread pizzas, breakfast wraps and pastries, chicken club sandwiches, falafel wraps, build-your-own bowls, samosas, grab-and-go snacks and kid-friendly options.

“We’re thrilled to welcome  Almadina to the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park ,” said Mayor Berry Vrbanovic. “Supporting local businesses is essential to building a strong, resilient economy, and  Almadina is a great example of the entrepreneurial spirit that makes Kitchener special. For more than 30 years, this family-run business has been part of our community, and now they’ll help fuel a landmark recreation centre designed for everyone to connect, compete and belong.”

Almadina operates four locations in Waterloo Region, including at the Kitchener Market, and is known for fresh, healthy Mediterranean-inspired food made with locally sourced ingredients whenever possible. Their commercial kitchen allows them to scale production to meet the demands of tournaments, events and busy periods at the Cowan Recreation Centre.

“This community has supported us for decades, and we’re excited to bring our fresh menu and our commitment to great customer experience to a space that will serve families, athletes and visitors in the years to come,” said  Abdullah Lawendy, owner of  Almadina. “We look forward to offering food that is healthy,  flavourful and made with care.”

When the facility opens late this year, the on-site food service is expected to  operate 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. seven days a week. The first year of operation will act as a pilot period to monitor demand and adjust hours as needed to support sustainable operations and accessible pricing.
Almadina will also offer catering for meetings and events inside the facility and will introduce seasonal menu rotations as the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park  grows and evolves.
For updates and more information, visit  Kitchener.ca/crc.
Corporate Communications and Marketing  City of Kitchener  media@kitchener.ca
